issue_context.title: Insteon 2448A7 USB PLM Often Not Found
issue_context.body:
### The problem

My Insteon 2448A7 USB PLM appears to be randomly assigned a USB port each time the system starts. Usually USB0, USB1, or USB2. My integration uses USB0 and does not work if another USB port is assigned. There needs to be a way to force the assignment of the 2448A7 USB PLM to a specific assignment that the Insteon integration can find, or for the integration to figure out and use whatever was assigned.
This issue has been going on for much longer than a year. I try to update the HA OS regularly.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.08.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

comments:
Hey there @teharris1, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`insteon`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L537) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

I'm not sure if this will resolve your problem, but using the serial by-id entry for the PLM worked for me. 

From your info  '/dev/serial/by-id/usb-FTDI_FT232R_USB_UART_AK05ZAYX-if00-port0' would likely work. Mine was similar but the K05ZAYX differed.  

In my case I had migrated my HA to a new physical host and since then the Insteon integration never really worked reliably. I decided to try removing the Insteon integration and re-add it. Upon re-install, the integration asked for the PLM port, and instead of using /dev/ttyUSB1, I decided to try the the longer by-id entry, which worked. I was expecting all the Insteon devices and entities to be have new names, assuming they would be new devices that conflict with the old devices,  but surprisingly everything stayed the same and even the automations still worked. 

Hopefully this will help someone out, because it was really frustrating for me and the the Insteon integration documentation doesn't mention this.
Thanks DiscoJeff. I'll (nervously) give that a try in the next week or so when I have a moment. Hopefully all my names will stay the same, too.

Short answer: No luck with a pain-free reinstallation of Insteon

Long answer: Your question inspired me to try deleting the Insteon integration and reinstall it. When I deleted it, Home Assistant said I needed to restart the system. Instead of doing so first, I went ahead and reinstalled the integration and used "/dev/serial/by-id/usb-FTDI_FT232R_USB_UART_AK05ZAYX-if00-port0" for the address of the USB PLM (which I got from HA Settings/System/Hardware/All Hardware/whatever-TTYUSBx-ID-the-USB-was-currently-using). I restarted HA. Home Assistant may have found the Insteon USB PLM for that one restart, but I didn't check. Instead I checked all my Insteon devices and found they were all renamed to the default names. This meant I'd need to rename them and/or my scripts, etc. I don't have time to do that now, so I restored the most recent full backup.

FYI, I'm up to date with all the Home Assistant updates for my Raspberry Pi4 system:

Home Assistant 2022.10.5
Supervisor 2022.10.0
Operating System 9.3
Frontend 20221010.0 - latest

FYI, the patch that was released allows for the user to change the USB port of the Insteon PLM. So if you previously had `/dev/ttyUSB0`, you can now go to `Settings` -> `Devices & Services` -> `Insteon` -> `Configure`.  From there you will see a new menu that says `Change the PLM configuration`. From here you can change the port to the underlying port such as `/dev/serial/by-id/usb-FTDI_FT232R_USB_UART_AK05ZAYX-if00-port0` without needing to reinstall. It will require you to restart HA however.
